Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 1 (Form 1040 line 15)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 1: "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 15" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), i.e. taxable income.
THIS IS THE POST-EXCLUSION FIGURE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. form2555 /schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion and /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction carry Form 2555 lines 45 and 50 into income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome and taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra, so on a gate-true return /taxableIncome is ALREADY reduced by the exclusion. A reader who assumes line 15 is gross of the exclusion will build this line wrong and the worksheet will subtract the exclusion twice.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (/taxableIncome is floored at zero and rounded at its own line).

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a (Form 2555 lines 45 and 50)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 2a: "Enter the amount from your (and your spouse's if filing jointly) Form 2555, lines 45 and 50" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
A ONE-TERM READ, ON PURPOSE. form2555 /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a is a fact whose entire job is to be this line: line 45 (the housing exclusion plus the foreign earned income exclusion, NET of the line-44 deductions allocable to excluded income) plus line 50 (the housing DEDUCTION). It is NOT form2555 /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911, which is section 911(a)(1) alone (Form 2555 line 42, for Form 8960 line 13), and it is NOT /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions, which is Form 2441's figure and is GROSS of line 44. Either substitution would silently drop a term.
THE NETTING TRAP: this figure ARRIVES already net of Form 2555 line 44, so line 2c below subtracts ONLY line 2b. Line 2b is a DIFFERENT quantity — line 44 is above-the-line deductions ALLOWED in figuring AGI, line 2b is deductions and exclusions DISALLOWED.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED — Form 2555 line 45 prints no "if zero or less, enter -0-" and can go negative when the allocable deductions exceed the exclusions. The floor in this chain lives on line 2c, where the worksheet prints it.

Fact.Name: Whether this return completes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet
Fact.Description:
The worksheet's own entry test, and the switch taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome reads to route Form 1040 line 16 here. THREE conjuncts, each printed:
1. THE POPULATION GATE — form2555 /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion. The worksheet is reached only from Form 2555. Gating on it is also the safety property form2555's own AGI-leg banner asks every consumer of the Form 2555 figures to supply or justify: the three section-911 FIGURES are bare compositions of the complete-safe entry aliases and are NOT gated, so a return that answers the amounts but leaves the attestation unanswered would otherwise reach this worksheet with an /agi that never moved — the exclusion subtracted nowhere, the rate stacking applied anyway. This conjunct is why that cannot happen.
2. THE CAUTION — "If Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 15, is zero, don't complete this worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). /taxableIncome is floored at zero, so "is zero" and "is zero or less" are the same test here and GreaterThan 0 is it.
3. THE AMOUNT — Form 2555 line 45 and line 50 each end "Complete the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 if you enter an amount on this line" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2555.pdf, page 3). So the worksheet opens on an AMOUNT, not on the gate: a filer who files Form 2555 and excludes nothing stays on the ordinary Form 1040 line-16 path.
THE ONE CORNER THIS CONJUNCT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH, disclosed rather than hidden: the printed trigger is per-line (an amount on line 45 OR on line 50), and this fact tests their SUM, because the sum is the only one of the three that form2555 exports. A return with line 45 exactly equal to the negative of line 50 would print as "enter the amount" on both lines and read as $0 here, so the worksheet would not be entered. It costs nothing: with line 2a at $0 the worksheet's line 2c is $0, line 3 equals line 1, line 5 is the tax on $0, and line 6 reduces to the ordinary tax on taxable income — the exact value the un-entered path already produces.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE ON AN UNANSWERED RETURN, and taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome's byte-identity depends on it: the gate is itself an IsComplete/Switch alias resolving Complete-false, /taxableIncome is Complete on every return that has one, and line 2a is a composition of four complete-safe $0 aliases. All three conjuncts are therefore Complete, so this fact is Complete false rather than Incomplete, and adding it as the first Case of that Switch moves no committed row.

Fact.Name: Itemized deductions or exclusions the filer could not claim because they relate to excluded income (worksheet line 2b)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's worksheet line 2b entry: "Enter the total amount of any itemized deductions or exclusions you couldn't claim because they are related to excluded income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
A WRITABLE RATHER THAN A COMPUTATION, AND RATHER THAN A HARD $0. The printed line asks the filer for a total the return does not otherwise carry: it is the DISALLOWED half of the allocation between excluded and non-excluded income, where Form 2555 line 44 is the ALLOWED half (above-the-line deductions actually taken in figuring AGI). Nothing in this dictionary computes it — no itemized-deduction allocation, no section 265 disallowance trace — and the worksheet itself asks for it as an entry, exactly as it asks for line 2a. A hard $0 would have been a silent claim that no such deductions exist, which is false for the itemizing member of this population; an entry says the number is the filer's and leaves the question askable (the application owes it, invariant #7).
NO CAP, NO CROSS-CHECK, and that matches the sibling Form 2555 entries in dictionary/ty2025/form2555.xml: this is a faithful taxpayer entry, floored at zero because the printed field is a "total amount" of deductions and a negative disallowance is not a thing the line can hold. It is deliberately NOT reconciled against Form 2555 line 44 or against scheduleA — that reconciliation is a future addition, and the knockout that refuses this whole population is what makes leaving it out a gap rather than a wrong number.
Optional — unanswered gives /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2b $0.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2b, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
= /writableForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2b when answered, else $0. The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom; the writable is never read directly.
DIRECTION OF THE $0 TAIL: taxpayer-ADVERSE, i.e. the conservative direction. A short line 2b leaves line 2c HIGH, so line 3 is HIGH and line 4 is HIGH; line 5 rises too, but by less, because the bracket schedule is convex — line 6 is tax(line 1 + line 2c) minus tax(line 2c), whose increments over line 2c are differences of marginal rates at line 1 + line 2c versus at line 2c, and those are non-negative. So an unanswered line 2b OVER-states the rate-stacked tax rather than under-stating it, and it keeps every committed scenario byte-identical, since no scenario answers it.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (the writable declares Min 0).

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2c (line 2a less line 2b, floored at zero)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 2c: "Subtract line 2b from line 2a. If zero or less, enter -0-" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
ONE SUBTRAHEND, AND ONLY ONE. Line 2a arrives ALREADY net of Form 2555 line 44, so nothing derived from line 44 may be subtracted again here; the netting trap is named on /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a and on form2555 /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a.
THIS IS WHERE THE CHAIN'S ONLY FLOOR LIVES, and it is printed here rather than on Form 2555 line 45 — line 45 deliberately carries no floor (see the fact), so a negative line 2a reaches this line and is floored to $0 exactly as the worksheet says.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3 (line 1 plus line 2c)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 3: "Add lines 1 and 2c" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). Taxable income with the excluded income put back — the amount whose tax line 4 figures, and the amount the QDCGT and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet substitute for their own line 1 when they are the route line 4 takes.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (both addends are).

Fact.Name: Tax-table midpoint of Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3
Fact.Description:
The tax-table midpoint of /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine3, exactly as /roundedTaxableIncome does for /taxableIncome and /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded does for /qdcgLine5. Drives worksheet line 4 (the tax on line 3).
STRUCTURAL TWIN of /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded (the engine has no taxOnAmount(x) primitive, so the row-width Switch is duplicated with its input swapped). The three Switches MUST stay in sync. Pinned to its siblings by the degenerate identity the node tests assert: when worksheet line 2c is $0, line 3 == line 1 == /taxableIncome, so this fact == /roundedTaxableIncome and worksheet line 4 == /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 4 by the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet (the unstarred route)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on worksheet line 3. /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 is a selector over this fact.
IT HAS TWO CONSUMERS AND THAT IS WHY IT EXISTS SEPARATELY: * /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4's Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet arm — the unstarred routes of "Use the Tax Table, Tax Computation Worksheet, Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet*, Schedule D Tax Worksheet*, or Form 8615, whichever applies" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37); * /feiQdcgLine24, the STARRED Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet's own line 24 ("Figure the tax on the amount on line 1"), because that worksheet's line 1 is the substituted Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3 — the same amount this fact already taxes. Reading line 24 off the selector instead would be a dependency cycle.
STRUCTURAL TWIN of /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome, which is itself the twin of taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome; /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine5 and /ordinaryTaxOnFeiWorksheetOrdinaryIncome are the other two in this module. THE FOUR SWITCHES IN THIS FILE MUST STAY IN SYNC.
ROUNDING: rounds at its own line, as the separately-figured tax it is; worksheet line 6 rounds again, idempotently.

Fact.Name: Capital gain excess (Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet starred footnote)
Fact.Description:
The starred footnote's capital gain excess: "To find out if you have a capital gain excess, subtract Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 15, from line 4 of your Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (line 10 of your Schedule D Tax Worksheet). If the result is more than zero, that amount is your capital gain excess" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
WHAT IT MEASURES, in one sentence, because the name does not say it: the amount by which the return's preferential-rate income exceeds its POST-exclusion taxable income. The substituted line 1 is larger than Form 1040 line 15 by the excluded income, so without this clawback the exclusion would shelter capital gain — the second worksheet would tax preferential income that the return's actual taxable income cannot hold.
THE MINUEND IS PASS-1 LINE 4. /qdcgLine4 is the shipping worksheet's line 2 + line 3, neither of which depends on line 1, so it is unchanged by the substitution and IS the "line 4 of your Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet" the footnote means after "complete the rest of that worksheet through line 4". Reading it off the MODIFIED line 4 would be a cycle.
THE SUBTRAHEND IS FORM 1040 LINE 15 ITSELF, not worksheet line 3. /qdcgLine1 is the module's own name for Form 1040 line 15 (= taxCalculations /taxableIncome); worksheet line 3 is line 15 PLUS the excluded income and would make this quantity structurally negative.
THE FLOOR IS THE FOOTNOTE'S "more than zero", and it is what lets the no-excess branch share these facts: at zero excess the two modified lines below equal the unmodified ones.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (floored here). Not rounded — it is an intermediate of the worksheet's line 2 and line 3, which are themselves unrounded amounts.

Fact.Name: Capital gain excess left over after modification (1)
Fact.Description:
Modification (2)'s "any of your capital gain excess not used in (1) above" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). Modification (1) reduces QDCGT line 3 by the excess but not below zero, so the amount it actually USES is the smaller of the excess and line 3, and what is left over is excess minus line 3, floored at zero.
WHY THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the excess is absorbed against the net capital gain FIRST and only the remainder touches qualified dividends. The footnote numbers the modifications and (2) names (1); reversing them would move income between the 15%/20% stack and the 0% stack in the wrong order on any return where both are present.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 1 (Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3, substituted)
Fact.Description: QDCGT line 1 on the second run: "However, if you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), enter the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 38). THIS SUBSTITUTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SECOND LINEAGE — it is the only line that differs from the shipping /qdcgLine1, and everything downstream differs only because of it.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 2 (qualified dividends, reduced by modification (2))
Fact.Description:
QDCGT line 2, "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 38), as modified by the starred footnote's modification (2): "Reduce (but not below zero) the amount you would otherwise enter on line 2 of your Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet ... by any of your capital gain excess not used in (1) above" (lines 2446-2447).
The printed line carries the footnote marker itself — "line 3a*" with "* If you are filing Form 2555, see the footnote in the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet before completing this line" (line 2509) — so the modification is not an inference.
Collapses to the unmodified /qdcgLine2 when there is no excess.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 3 (net capital gain, reduced by modification (1))
Fact.Description:
QDCGT line 3, the net capital gain — "Enter the smaller of line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D. If either line 15 or line 16 is blank or a loss, enter -0-" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 38) — as modified by the starred footnote's modification (1): "Reduce (but not below zero) the amount you would otherwise enter on line 3 of your Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet ... by your capital gain excess" (lines 2444-2445).
THE ONLY SCHEDULE D READ IN THIS WHOLE LINEAGE, and it is a READ: /qdcgLine3 is scheduleD /netCapitalGain, i.e. Schedule D lines 15 and 16. Modifications (3) and (4) touch Schedule D line 18 and the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet, which are inputs to the SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET and to nothing here — see the block banner.
Collapses to the unmodified /qdcgLine3 when there is no excess.

Starred QDCGT line 5 (ordinary-income slice)
Fact.Description: Subtract line 4 from line 1; if zero or less, enter 0.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 8
Fact.Description: Smaller of line 5 or line 7.

Fact.Description: Subtract line 8 from line 7. This amount is taxed at 0%.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 10
Fact.Description: Smaller of line 1 or line 4.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 11
Fact.Description: Amount from line 9.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 12
Fact.Description: Subtract line 11 from line 10.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 13 (15% breakpoint)
Fact.Description: Maximum 15%-rate amount for the filing status.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 14
Fact.Description: Smaller of line 1 or line 13.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 15
Fact.Description: Add lines 5 and 9.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 16
Fact.Description: Subtract line 15 from line 14; if zero or less, enter 0.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 17 (amount taxed at 15%)
Fact.Description: Smaller of line 12 or line 16.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 18 (tax at 15%)
Fact.Description: Multiply line 17 by 15% (0.15).

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 19
Fact.Description: Add lines 9 and 17.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 20 (amount taxed at 20%)
Fact.Description: Subtract line 19 from line 10.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 21 (tax at 20%)
Fact.Description: Multiply line 20 by 20% (0.20).

Fact.Name: Rounded ordinary income (starred QDCGT line 5)
Fact.Description: The tax-table midpoint of /feiQdcgLine5 (the starred worksheet's ordinary-income slice), exactly as /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded does for /qdcgLine5. Drives the starred line 22 (tax on line 5). STRUCTURAL TWIN of /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded (no taxOnAmount primitive); keep in sync.

Fact.Name: Ordinary-rate tax on the starred QDCGT's line 5
Fact.Description: The tax-rate-schedule tax on /feiWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded, i.e. the starred worksheet's line 22. STRUCTURAL TWIN of /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome, which is itself the twin of taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome and of /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute and /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine5 in this module. THE FOUR SWITCHES IN THIS FILE MUST STAY IN SYNC, and the bracket schedule below is character for character the one on /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome with the input re-pointed.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 22 (tax on line 5)
Fact.Description: Figure the tax on the amount on line 5 (Tax Table if < $100,000, else Tax Computation Worksheet) — i.e. /ordinaryTaxOnFeiWorksheetOrdinaryIncome.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 23 (worksheet tax)
Fact.Description: Add lines 18, 21, and 22.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 24 (tax on line 1)
Fact.Description:
Figure the tax on the amount on line 1. Line 1 here is the SUBSTITUTED line 1 — Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3 — so this line is exactly /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute, the unstarred route's own answer, and no fifth copy of the bracket schedule is needed.
THIS IS WHY THE UNSTARRED ROUTE HAD TO BE EXTRACTED FROM /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 rather than read off it: that fact is now the SELECTOR between the two routes, and a starred line 24 pointing at the selector would be a cycle.

Fact.Name: Starred QDCGT line 25 — the tax the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet puts on its line 4
Fact.Description:
The smaller of line 23 or line 24. The printed line names this worksheet's destination explicitly: "If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on the entry space on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 38).
THE COLLAPSE THAT MAKES THIS SAFE AS THE DEFAULT ARM of /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4: with lines 2 and 3 both zero, line 4 is zero, line 5 equals line 1, line 8 equals line 7 so line 9 is zero, line 10 is zero and lines 11, 12, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 follow it to zero — leaving line 23 = line 22 = the tax on line 1 = line 24, so line 25 IS line 24. A return with no qualified dividends and no net capital gain therefore gets the unstarred route's exact number through this arm, which is the same argument taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome makes for its own default arm.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE. UNROUNDED — line 18 and line 21 are rate products and the worksheet rounds at its destination, which for this run is Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 4.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 4 (the tax on line 3)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 4: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 3. Use the Tax Table, Tax Computation Worksheet, Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet*, Schedule D Tax Worksheet*, or Form 8615, whichever applies. See the instructions for Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16, to see which tax computation method applies" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). This fact is the SELECTOR among those routes; each route's arithmetic lives in its own fact.
THE SWITCH, ARM BY ARM, and the shape is deliberately the same one taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome uses for Form 1040 line 16, because line 4 is asking the same question about the same return. BOTH ARMS COMPUTE; neither is an upper bound and no route of this line is refused: * ARM 1 fires on scheduleD /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet — the Schedule D Tax Worksheet's own printed entry test — and takes scheduleD /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax, the STARRED SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET run on the substituted line 1 with all four of the footnote's modifications. The lineage and its block banner live in dictionary/ty2025/scheduleD.xml, where the worksheet it copies lives, because modifications (3) and (4) rewrite Schedule D's own lines 18 and 19. * ARM 2, the default, takes /feiQdcgLine25 — the STARRED Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, run on the substituted line 1 with the footnote's modifications (1) and (2). See the block banner above /feiCapitalGainExcess.
WHY THE DEFAULT ARM DOES NOT NEED A "has preferential income" TEST, which is the one thing a reader will want to add: with /qdcgLine2 and /qdcgLine3 both zero the starred QDCGT collapses term by term to the tax on its own line 1, i.e. to /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute (the argument is written out on /feiQdcgLine25). So a return with neither qualified dividends nor a net capital gain gets the unstarred route's exact number through arm 2, and adding a gate would only re-derive it. Form 8615's GATE ships as form8615:/mustFileForm8615 (a knockout: the child's return is refused, not computed here); the computation itself — the child's tax at the parent's rate — is not built, so no route of this line ever selects it.
ROUNDING: the Round wraps the Switch, so it lands on whichever arm fires, and it is the real rounding point on BOTH arms. /feiQdcgLine25 and scheduleD /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax are each deliberately unrounded, because each one's PRINTED destination is this line — "don't enter this amount on the entry space on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet" appears at the foot of both worksheets (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 38 and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16) — exactly as the shipping /qdcgLine25 and scheduleD /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax send theirs to Form 1040 line 16 and are rounded there. Anyone who adds a Round to either of those two facts double-rounds a Form 2555 return's tax.

Fact.Name: Tax-table midpoint of Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2c
Fact.Description:
The tax-table midpoint of /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2c. Drives worksheet line 5 (the tax on line 2c).
THE $100,000 SPLIT THIS FACT ENCODES IS PRINTED ON WORKSHEET LINE 5 ITSELF, which is the one place the worksheet states the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet boundary in its own words: "If the amount on line 2c is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure this tax. If the amount on line 2c is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). The generic twin already had that boundary; line 5 is the printed authority for it.
STRUCTURAL TWIN of /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded. The three Switches MUST stay in sync.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 5 (the tax on line 2c)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 5: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 2c. If the amount on line 2c is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure this tax. If the amount on line 2c is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
LINE 5 HAS NO STARRED ROUTES AND THAT IS WHY IT NEEDS NO SCOPE CARVE-OUT. Unlike line 4, which offers the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, the Schedule D Tax Worksheet and Form 8615, line 5 names ONLY the Tax Table and the Tax Computation Worksheet. So this Switch is line 5 in full for every return that reaches the worksheet, including the preferential-rate returns the knockout below refuses.
REPOINTED ONTO THE SHARED RATE-SCHEDULE KERNEL. This was the SEVENTH copy of the ordinary-tax ladder, and K12's own measurement said six: it carried the full outer filing-status Switch with all 76 Dollar literals written out, while the six K12 named were re-pointed at taxCalculations /taxRateScheduleBracketTop* and /taxRateScheduleBase*. It now reads the same twelve kernel facts, in the shipped formulation lifted from /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome with only the input path swapped: 948 lines of Derived became 153, and the 76 literals became 19 kernel dependencies.
THE DIFFERENTIAL, IN VALUE AND IN KIND. Value: the 76 literals sat in 4 filing-status arms of 19 slots each, and the template's 19 kernel dependencies stand in exactly those slots — all 76 (status, slot) pairs were checked against the kernel facts' own per-status values and all 76 matched, with the seven bracket rates and the Add/Multiply/Subtract counts identical per arm. Kind: the pre-edit outer Switch had four filing-status cases (MFJ, QSS, HOH, Single, MFS) and NO unconditional fallthrough, and each kernel fact has that same shape and no fallthrough — which is why the kernel was authored without one — so a return whose filing status is unanswerable resolves Incomplete on both formulations.
STRUCTURAL TWIN of /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome — and the twin is now a SHARED READ rather than a copied bracket schedule, which is the point of the re-point: the two Switches can no longer drift apart on a parameter, because there is only one statement of each parameter left. What still has to stay in sync is the SHAPE (the seven-case bracket ladder and its rates), not the numbers. ROUNDING: rounds at its own line; worksheet line 6 rounds again, idempotently.

Fact.Name: Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 6 — the tax a Form 2555 filer reports on Form 1040 line 16
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 6: "Subtract line 5 from line 4. Enter the result. If zero or less, enter -0-. Also include this amount on the entry space on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). Fills the contract of the same path.
CONSUMER: taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome, whose FIRST Switch arm fires on /entersForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheet. First rather than last is required, not stylistic: the QDCGT and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet are what worksheet line 4 may USE, so a Form 2555 return must be diverted before those arms are reached, and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet's own line 47 redirects away from Form 1040 line 16 for exactly this population (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16).
SCOPE: ALL FOUR REPRESENTABLE ROUTES of line 4 — the Tax Table, the Tax Computation Worksheet, the starred QUALIFIED DIVIDENDS AND CAPITAL GAIN TAX WORKSHEET and the starred SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET (scheduleD /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax). See the block banner above. Nothing this fact can be asked is refused: /knockoutForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetPreferentialRate no longer guards the SDTW population, and the value on that population is the worksheet's own answer, not a bound on it. Form 8615 is unreachable for want of any representation in this dictionary, not by a refusal here.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (line 6 floors at zero). Rounded at this line, the printed entry line; lines 4 and 5 are separately-figured taxes and round at their own lines, so this Round is idempotent and is kept for the entry-line identity.
